changes.before: When enchanting raises an item's rarity, the player pays the upgrade cost difference they skipped: what the item's Blacksmith upgrades from its starting level to its current level cost at the new rarity, minus what they cost at the old rarity (gold + gear-upgrade materials). Every route (upgrade then enchant, or enchant then upgrade) costs the same total. Each item stores one extra saved number: the item level it dropped or was bought at. How it is worked out: for each level from the item's starting level to its current level, (normal Blacksmith upgrade cost at the new rarity - cost at the old rarity), gold and gear materials. Discount (LOCKED - USER DECISION 2026-11-01): each level uses the Blacksmith gold discount of the Blacksmith level needed to reach that level, 3% x (ceil(level / 10) - 1) - levels 2-10 0%, 11-20 3%, 21-30 6% ... 81-90 24%, 91-99 27% - NOT the player's current discount. Each level's cost is rounded down to whole gold first (economy_framework 19), so the fee is always whole gold. Example, Common -> Epic, item level 1 -> 99: 1H 22,201g, 2H 33,299g, Body 17,763g (+196 gear materials, materials are never discounted). Downgrading an item below its starting level lowers the starting level to the new level. Items that existed before this is built start at their current level, so they never owe a fee (USER-CONFIRMED 2026-11-01; accepted side effect: dismantling such items returns no gear-upgrade materials, only the +1 for Rare and up).

changes.before: Destroys the item. Gives NO gold (selling = gold, dismantling = materials). Gear materials are refunded TIER BY TIER (LOCKED - USER DECISION 2026-11-01): for each material tier, refund = round down (refund % from row 50 x the gear materials of THAT tier that the normal recipe charges for this item from its starting level to its current level at its current rarity), paid in that same tier. The T5 part (levels 81-99) is paid as the same number of T4, never T5 (E4). Plus 1 extra gear material if the item's STARTING rarity is Rare or higher (equipment_schema 19, the same basis as the sell rule, economy_framework 14), in the tier of the item's current level band (L1-20 T1, L21-40 T2, L41-60 T3, L61-99 T4); enchanting an item up to Rare never earns the +1. Example: Common Gloves upgraded L1 -> 61, dismantled at Blacksmith L10 (50%): spent 19 T1 / 20 T2 / 20 T3 / 1 T4, refund 9 T1 / 10 T2 / 10 T3 / 0 T4. Essences = 1 per bonus line (numbers or bonus passive) at that line's rarity (tiers 1-2 Uncommon, tier 3 Rare, tier 4+ Epic; a passive uses its minimum rarity), capped at the Blacksmith's extraction rarity (row 50). Common items (no lines) give gear materials only. Shop-bought items give nothing (no materials, no Essences).
